en.title: Diablo 4 Switch 2 Port Reportedly Arriving Mid-September
en.summary: A fresh leak suggests Blizzard's action RPG, Diablo 4, is finally making its way to the Nintendo Switch 2. The rumored release date places it in mid-September, but with a surprising physical release detail.
en.body:
The hellish landscapes of **Diablo 4** may soon be accessible on the go, as a new leak points to a Nintendo Switch 2 release. According to reports, Blizzard is preparing to launch the critically acclaimed action RPG on Nintendo's next-generation handheld sometime in mid-September.

This potential port arrives more than three years after **Diablo 4** first unleashed its demons upon PC, PlayStation, and Xbox in June 2023. The leak, attributed to the usually reliable Dealabs user billbil-kun, indicates a price point of $69.99 / £62.99 / €69.99 for the Switch 2 version. Notably, the physical release is said to contain only a digital download code, with no physical game media or even a card inside the box. While an exact date remains elusive, the third week of September, specifically the 15th or 18th, is being cited as the target window. It is currently unclear if the upcoming **Lord of Hatred** expansion will be bundled with this new release.

## Sanctuary's Next Frontier

Whispers of **Diablo 4** gracing Nintendo hardware have circulated for some time, bolstered by appearances on various ratings boards. Rod Fergusson, who previously oversaw the **Diablo** franchise, had previously commented that a Switch version was "something to look at," suggesting internal consideration for such a port. The Indonesian Game Rating System (IGRS) even listed **Diablo IV: Lord of Hatred** for the Nintendo Switch in April 2026, further fueling speculation. Given the technical advancements expected with the Switch 2, it's logical that any potential port would target this newer hardware to ensure a smoother experience, rather than the current Switch model.

## Fan Anticipation and Potential Hurdles

This leak is bound to excite fans who have been eager to experience **Diablo 4**'s deep endgame and compelling progression on a portable device. The game, despite its age, maintains a dedicated player base, with its second major expansion launching in April and the much-discussed secret cow level finally being discovered earlier this year. However, the prospect of a physical release containing only a code raises questions about Nintendo's strategy for its next console and the practicalities of porting such a large, live-service game. Players will be watching closely to see how Blizzard handles the technical challenges and pricing for this new platform.

## What's Next

With Gamescom on the horizon later this month, an official announcement regarding **Diablo 4**'s Switch 2 presence could be imminent. Until then, players can continue to explore the world of Sanctuary on its existing platforms, while anticipating further details on this rumored portable version.

content_raw: Blizzard will launch Diablo 4 on Nintendo Switch 2 next month, a fresh leak has revealed. As reported by Dealabs ' ever-reliable billbil-kun, the Switch 2 version of Diablo 4 will arrive in mid-September priced at $69.99 / £62.99 / €69.99, more than three years after the game first debuted on PC, PlayStation and Xbox back in June 2023. Alongside a digital launch via the eShop, the game's Switch 2 port will also be released with a physical edition — though this will just contain a digital download code in an otherwise empty box. (Yes, there's not even a Game-Key Card here.) An exact release date isn't yet available, though it's reported that the game will launch during the third week of September, on either Tuesday 15 or Friday 18. It's also unclear whether the game's Lord of Hatred expansion will also be included. Today's leak follows months of expectation that Blizzard is prepping an official Switch 2 launch for the game, which has previously popped up on a couple of ratings boards. Exactly when the company will formally announce the port remains to be seen, though we are now just weeks away from the annual Gamescom extravaganza, which once again takes place in Cologne, Germany later this month. While Diablo 4 may be several years' old at this point, the game still enjoys a dedicated playerbase and received its second big expansion only in April. In May, the game's secret cow level was finally discovered — though after such a long build-up, some players were left a little disappointed . "Diablo 4 is a stunning sequel with near perfect endgame and progression design that makes it absolutely excruciating to put down," we wrote in IGN's Diablo 4 review , which returned a devilish 9/10 score.
